To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed and tested a standards based assessment framework and pipeline that can be used to assess learning in a STEM domain (engineering) and a STEM learning topic (Minecraft).

we have developed a standards based assessment tool for a learning environment that can be used to assess learning in engineering education, that the tool is usable by students, and that it can be used to analyze learning in a Minecraft focus session.

the PLAY environment was a highly positive learning experience for the children, that the children were able to apply the engineering standards in the NGSS to their Minecraft challenges, that their application of standards was consistent by age, and that their discussion of Minecraft topics varied consistently by their age.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of engineering practices in the NGSS, and with the domain of Minecraft, a popular online construction game.
the Science and Engineering Practice (SEP) of applying the engineering design process, which is a key component of engineering education.
the following NGSS Science and engineering practices (Figure 1) Asking questions (for science) and defining problems (for engineering).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NGSS sets performance expectation for each disciplinary core ideas (DCI) based on age level, Science and Engineering Practices (SEP), Disciplinary Core Ideas, and Crosscutting concepts (CC).
the Minecraft game is a very good example of a learning tool that can help students learn engineering standards.
the NGSS Science and engineering practices are the skills that scientists and engineers use in order to conduct scientific investigations and engineering design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it showed that the NGSS Science and Enginering Practices are a good starting point for developing a machine learning based assessment tool for STEM education.

we were able to show that the PLAY! platform can be used to support engineering learning, that we were able, with the help of our students and a small focus group, to identify engineering standards, and that the machine learning classification system and natural language analysis tools can be used to assess student learning in the domain and on the topic.
we were able to develop an automated assessment pipeline that can be used to analyze student work in a participatory learning environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to develop a computational assessment pipeline for NGSS standards and domain topics.
computational tools such as machine learning and natural language processing are promising for use in engineering assessment.
it is possible to develop a computational assessment system for NGSS aligned learning using the tools of computational linguistics.
